translation_notes: prefixes: SH->sh -- but SH (imported by the region's own context line, `from etk.knowledge_graph.shacl import SH, SHACL, SHACLOntoConverter`) is never used as a term anywhere in test_cnode's own body: the region's only RDF operations are the two `rdflib.URIRef('http://example.org/...')` calls, so there is nothing to bind a prefix to. SH/SHACL stay plain (unused) imports, same reasoning as johnjung/metadata_converters' BASE in this stratum: a mixed import list is legal, only names actually used as namespaces become prefixes.

`rdflib.URIRef('http://example.org/Person')` -> `<http://example.org/Person>`, dropping the constructor call entirely rather than keeping `rdflib.<...>` (the mechanical draft's mistake): an absolute-IRI island is a term, not a call, so `rdflib.` in front of it is not legal syntax -- the transpiler rejects it. No @base is in scope, and no prefix is declared or needed for an absolute IRI.

Restoring the binding (AGENT_BATCH's 163-regions case): test_cnode's `self` needs only the three unittest assert methods it calls (assertIsInstance x3, assertEqual, assertNotEqual) -- verified against the pinned commit that TestSHACLOntoConverter carries no setUp/fixture this test relies on -- so a plain `unittest.TestCase()` instance is a faithful `self`, not an invented stand-in. Appended demo() (identical on both sides) calls test_cnode(case) and returns a sentinel string: the region's whole effect is raising on a failing assertion, so 'did not raise' needs an explicit observable or run_pair reports 'nothing observable to compare'.

etk.knowledge_graph.node/etk.knowledge_graph.shacl are not installed (etk is not a pip package here): etk_context.py copies Node/URI/BNode/Literal/SHACLOntoConverter.__init__/.cnode/.class_nodes verbatim from the pinned commit. LiteralType is stubbed to its URI-subclass identity only (the real class is a ~130-line regex-based xsd/rdf datatype validator, not reached by test_cnode at all), and SHACL/Graph are stubbed to what SHACLOntoConverter.__init__ touches (a no-op .bind()) -- none of these three are exercised by the region under test.
